title: The Worked Strips — the barley fields east of Low Kiln, Sill
caption: The ground east of Low Kiln drawn at walking scale, the chart the lived days have fallen on from the planting of Seed through the cutting and dressing of Grain to the wool-covered grain of Smoke: five long rutted plots with their furrows and a flood stone a woman swept around, the clay-heavy Slip Brook coming down behind the drying racks, the reedbeds standing grey in the ruts where the barley stood, the Ilm along the head of the chart with its landing and punt, and the river road above the strips. Low Kiln, the Vail roof and its smoke, the drying racks and the Cross are drawn faint at the western edge for neighbourhood only; the Weir lies a league upriver, Mud End and Greybank downriver, Reedholt away through the marsh. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Smoke, with compass, a hundred-pace scale, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the arm that knows a bundle's weight and no slate its price, the clay-heavy rise that took a woman from the end of nineteen steps and was called weather, and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out — described in the margin and marked nowhere, for a mark would be a figure and no figure stands. An engraved ear of barley with its top grain gone sits in the margin.
